summary: This article explains how potters knead, shape, dry, fire, and decorate clay to create pottery that is both a useful craft and a beautiful art form across many cultures.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Pottery: Shaping Clay into Art” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: to press and fold a soft material over and over with the hands
a hard material made by baking clay at a very high temperature
to add color, patterns, or designs to make something look more attractive

challengeTerms.def: a delicate, nearly translucent type of ceramic, historically made famous by Chinese artisans
skill and care in making something by hand
having many small, carefully arranged details

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that pottery is just as much an art as it is a useful craft? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why kneading and firing are both important steps in making pottery.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review knead, ceramic, and decorate, and let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses porcelain, craftsmanship, and intricate to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
